Yarn Classic workspace builds now share captured artifact/report planning and stage composition, while native acquisition, version projection and packing remain manager-owned. See that reference for its narrower evidence and remaining gaps. pnpm workspace builds also consume the common artifact/report planner, with pnpm-owned importer projection and native archive creation. Their isolated CLI acceptance remains pending.

Every workspace member is packaged as its own snapshot archive, under its package name and a version derived from its own version. A root without private: true is packaged too; a private root is not. On 2026-10-10 the maintainer decided that members which cannot be packaged that way fail with an error that names every affected member and its path, and are never skipped silently. Two conditions fail: a package name is used by more than one member, or by a publishable root and a member; a member's version is latest. npm membership is resolved first, before any dependency is acquired, so both conditions are reported together in one error with the stable code NPM_WORKSPACE_MEMBER_NAMES. Paths are relative to the workspace root. For the EX-020 npm-member-names variation: NPM_WORKSPACE_MEMBER_NAMES: npm workspace members need distinct package names and real versions to be packaged package name "@oyzu-example/core" is used by "." (publishable workspace root), "packages/core" version "latest" is not a package version: "test", "test/installation" Remedy: rename packages so each name is used once, or mark the workspace root "private": true so the root is not packaged; give each listed member a semver "version" such as "0.0.0" in its package.json; "private": true on a member does not exclude it, because every member is packaged. In oyzu build this text appears inside the npm dependency preparation failed diagnostic. Nothing has been acquired, no artifact is produced and the source is unchanged. oyzu run workspace tasks resolve the same membership and stop with the same error; static oyzu run list does not resolve membership and is unaffected. To recover: Rename members so each package name is used once. When the root only coordinates the workspace, "private": true on the root also works, because a private root is not packaged. The nestjs/nest repository has this shape: its root and packages/core are both named @nestjs/core. Give each latest member a semver version, such as 0.0.0. Marking the member "private": true does not help: private members are packaged like any other, and excluding a member from packaging is not implemented. The puppeteer/puppeteer repository has this shape: its test and test/installation members are already private and versioned latest. npm itself refuses members that share a name. Oyzu takes those members from npm's report and lists them with the other problems. If npm cannot list the remaining members after excluding them, which happens when a duplicate's path contains glob syntax, the error says that other members were not checked. Other invalid member names or versions still fail with npm workspace requires a valid native name/version, and a publishable root with an invalid name or version with Publishable npm workspace root requires a valid native name/version. This check covers npm workspaces only; pnpm and Yarn keep their existing checks. node --test tooling/test-npm-member-names.mjs covers the error text, private roots and npm's duplicate report with the provisioned npm; python tooling/test-npm-workspaces.py runs the npm-member-names variation through native acquisition, and the compiled-CLI node-workspaces group builds it. None of these has been run for this change yet, and the nestjs/nest and puppeteer/puppeteer repositories have not been re-run; see implementation status.

CLI reference Published from the canonical docs/reference/nuget-sessions.md file. Features marked experimental remain experimental; check support limitations before relying on them. Oyzu can automatically prepare native dotnet restore and dotnet build with a session-scoped NuGet credential plugin. This is an opt-in client prototype with a simulated local agent in its proof. It is not the captured .NET oyzu build builder (see .NET builds, which does not use sessions yet), platform login, or CI identity implementation.

Provision a .NET 8 SDK and configure an agent endpoint in user or administrative Oyzu configuration: [nuget] sessionEndpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:43199/session" The port is illustrative. The existing configuration cascade resolves the setting. Project/local/invocation origins and profile selection cannot choose the endpoint. It must be numeric-loopback HTTP without credentials, query or fragment. The setting is absent by default; removing it restores standalone launch behavior. User configuration remains excluded in CI by existing rules. oyzu exec -- /usr/share/dotnet/dotnet restore --locked-mode oyzu exec -- /usr/share/dotnet/dotnet build --no-restore # With provisioned dotnet on PATH: eval "$(oyzu activate bash)" dotnet build Linux with the .NET 8 SDK is the measured platform. Native Windows/macOS execution is unqualified; Windows managed-session shell shims are not implemented. Only restore and build are supported managed operations. Native help/version/info and installed-SDK/runtime listing bypass session creation. Other operations fail explicitly rather than bypassing admission. In particular, dotnet nuget push is not offered; artifact publication belongs to oyzu publish. Native .NET publish also remains outside this bounded command surface, even though it normally prepares application output rather than uploading a package.

Every supported launch asks the agent for admission before compiling its adapter or starting native project work. This includes build --no-restore with already restored packages. The request contains directory, tool and arguments; the local directory is a context hint, not verified source ownership. The experimental response supplies feed, credentialScope, username and credentialEndpoint. Feed and scope must share an origin, the scope must end in /, and the feed must lie below that path. URLs must be credential-free HTTP(S) without query/fragment. The credential endpoint is numeric-loopback HTTP. The first adapter supports one feed and one same-origin credential scope; cross-origin service resources require separate qualification. A literal semicolon in the feed is rejected because NuGet interprets restore sources as a list. Rust compiles Oyzu's bundled minimal C# plugin using the already selected SDK in a temporary directory, with package sources cleared for that compilation. No third-party package or extra language runtime is required. It stages a temporary credential-free NuGet config and session metadata and selects the plugin using NUGET_NETCORE_PLUGIN_PATHS. NuGet starts the plugin and requests credentials over its native process protocol. The plugin obtains the password from the admitted session only for a URI inside the allowed scope. Managed mode replaces restore configuration/sources through MSBuild global properties, clears additional project restore sources, replaces native plugin-path selection, and removes the environment credential override for the managed source name. The fixture explicitly includes a conflicting project RestoreSources property to verify the approved feed wins. Project files are not edited. Other native project build settings stay native-owned, but this prototype does not merge custom source mappings, multiple feeds, custom settings files or provider plugins. Explicit source/config overrides on the command line are rejected. Passwords travel through native process memory and NuGet plugin pipes, never through the generated settings, launcher arguments or launcher environment. The session locator is access-sensitive; the laboratory transport is not a production authenticated IPC channel. Native build code can access process state; this is not hostile-code containment. Upstream identity permissions enforce read-only access.

Native output and exit status follow oyzu exec; global --json retains captured native streams in its structured result. The launcher disables MSBuild node reuse for the child. Normal native package/HTTP caches remain enabled. Temporary plugin source, build output, settings and metadata are removed after normal success or failure. Project outputs, lock files and native caches remain native-owned. Abrupt parent termination cleanup and compilation caching are deferred. NATIVE_SESSION_* errors identify shared authority/admission failures. NUGET_SESSION_INVALID identifies malformed feed/session data; NUGET_SESSION_PREPARE requires a working .NET 8 SDK and local reference packs; NUGET_ROUTING_CONFLICT rejects competing source/config arguments; NUGET_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED identifies a command outside restore/build. Agent outage/denial fails before native work, with no direct fallback or offline grant. Plugin failures return generic errors rather than upstream response bodies. Argument checks are a bounded supported surface, not a complete MSBuild parser. Arbitrary project targets/network calls, inherited custom MSBuild behavior and additional SDK/runtime versions are not qualified. Production platform and CI identity integration are deferred. No Oyzu schema version changes; NuGet's plugin protocol version belongs to NuGet. See the integration proof.

CLI reference Published from the canonical docs/reference/oci-indices.md file. Features marked experimental remain experimental; check support limitations before relying on them. Experimental captured builds automatically assemble one OCI index artifact for a complete selected family of platform images. No additional packaging setting is needed. Individual images and their test/quality evidence remain in the bundle. This implements image aggregation; it does not itself provide execution, publishing, signing or release authorization. Toolchain platform selection separately admits matching language execution images.

For a Dockerfile containing FROM scratch and COPY: builds: image: uses: docker/image platforms: [linux/x86_64, linux/arm64] oyzu run list oyzu build image --plan oyzu build image oyzu inspect dist Provision the existing Linux Docker toolchain and rootless BuildKit worker before building, as described in Docker image inputs. The image builder currently admits Linux amd64/arm64 assembly; foreign-platform RUN still fails without supported target execution. Windows/macOS host support does not establish native Windows/macOS container execution. Tool or image installation is not performed automatically. run list retains logical builder tasks. The captured plan adds an engine-owned assemble-index action after the image package actions; it is not a configurable builder or a separate development task. The executable plan retained by a build shows that action. Read-only --plan previews declared variants and relationships; generated aggregation actions remain unresolved until preparation.

Aggregation requires at least two platform variants of one logical target, with every member selected. Corresponding image outputs must have the same unique output name and version. Different non-platform axes form separate groups: two runtime versions each receive their own complete platform index. A target that declares one platform retains just its image. A dependency selection containing only part of a larger platform family does not invent a partial index. See matrix selection. The derived target ID uses the logical family, oci-index, output name and remaining axes through the existing portable-name encoding. Read IDs and paths from the plan rather than reconstructing normalized names. Each aggregate produces: A kind: "oci-index" artifact with the common image version and media type application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json. A file at dist/<aggregate-id>/any/<family>-<version>.oci.tar; the index spans its member platforms, so it is placed under any (see the bundle layout). A file digest and size, plus ociDigest identifying the root OCI index for eventual registry publication. The aggregate target uses builder oyzu/oci-index, retains non-platform variant axes and has platform: null. The assembly action likewise has targetPlatform: null and records the CLI host as its execution platform. Null means a collection of platforms, not platform-independent application output. The selection extension continues to list selected source variants; the derived aggregate is additionally present in plan/manifest targets. Its oyzu.dev/oci-index extension binds the family and exact required artifact IDs, producers and platforms. These are changes to experimental v1alpha1 records. Consumers must handle derived targets and nullable aggregate platforms; ordinary image targets/actions still require concrete platforms. Synthetic schema fixtures check the record shape, not successful execution.

All required image package actions must succeed before assembly. The engine checks each retained file's hash/size, native OCI closure, publication digest and platform. It writes a self-contained archive containing unchanged image manifest/config/layer bytes, deduplicated blobs and a sorted index. Stable headers and ordering make the archive independent of input enumeration order for the same image inputs. Assembly reads archives without extraction and performs no network access or subprocess execution. It runs in the CLI process, with a 10 GiB output archive limit and at most 256 inputs. It does not claim container isolation or process-level CPU, memory or timeout enforcement. The temporary archive is verified before publication without replacing an existing destination. Assembly errors fail the action and retain the build's failure evidence under the normal bundle lifecycle. A failed platform blocks the aggregate; successful peer image artifacts may remain available for inspection. An index cannot silently omit the failed platform. Repair the native failure or invalid input and rebuild; do not treat a surviving peer image as a complete matrix result. oyzu inspect dist checks exact index membership against the recorded required image artifacts and successful producers. It rejects a valid but incomplete index and a successful bundle missing a planned index. Inspecting the standalone OCI archive verifies its own content closure; it cannot establish the build's required platform set without the bundle. Neither form authenticates the builder or grants production publication rights.

Local Rust tests cover deterministic bytes, shared-blob deduplication, input preservation, malformed/missing content, platform/digest mismatch, duplicate platforms, no-overwrite behavior, complete-family planning, failed prerequisites and bundle membership checks. These use independently authored OCI fixtures, not native container execution. Schema checks reject missing member requirements and null platforms on ordinary targets/actions. The Linux captured Docker suite passed actual amd64/arm64 scratch builds, their complete index, repeated archive identity, CLI inspection and a platform-specific hook failure that blocks the index in Docker job 110864668852 at revision 1b8bd3c. This proves copy-only image assembly, not target application execution. Full EX-027/050 acceptance still requires the complete policy/ABI/cache cases and platform verification; the new producer execution checks are tracked in toolchain platforms. General platform ABI/features negotiation and registry publishing remain unfinished. The archive follows the OCI image index specification: its index references platform-specific image manifests by digest.

CLI reference Published from the canonical docs/reference/oci-sessions.md file. Features marked experimental remain experimental; check support limitations before relying on them. This isolated prototype adds automatic session preparation for explicitly provisioned Helm and BuildKit clients. It implements client mechanics only; a production agent, account login, policy evaluator and OCI tool installation are not supplied. The proof record distinguishes simulator behavior from product code and measured results.

The user or an administrator configures a numeric-loopback HTTP endpoint in their existing Oyzu configuration file. For the laboratory: [oci] sessionEndpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:43199/session" Use the normal configuration cascade. Project/local/invocation sources cannot set this endpoint; the launch adapter checks its resolved authority. User settings are excluded in CI by existing configuration behavior. This is a local developer prototype, not CI workload authentication. OYZU_USER_CONFIG can select an absolute user file for isolated testing, without changing its authority. The endpoint must have no username, password, query or fragment. Authentication of this IPC connection remains future work; use only the disposable fixture agent. The setting does not create an authenticated platform account. Removing it returns the existing standalone behavior; an absent setting is not a governed denial.

With provisioned native executables and the prototype CLI: oyzu exec -- /usr/local/bin/helm pull oci://registry.example.com/charts/sample --version 0.1.0 oyzu exec -- /usr/local/bin/buildctl --addr tcp://builder.example.com:1234 build --frontend dockerfile.v0 --local context=. --local dockerfile=. --output type=local,dest=dist These are invocation-shape examples, not reachable fixture endpoints. The reproduction harness supplies local registries and builders. Configure appropriate TLS independently for real transports. Supported managed Helm command-first forms are pull, dependency and template; BuildKit requires a build argument. This is not a comprehensive native argument parser or general Docker CLI adapter. Native credential override flags (--registry-config, --username, --password) are rejected. push=true is rejected; publication remains an oyzu publish path. Help/version do not request an access session. Other executables retain ordinary standalone execution. On Unix, normal shell environment composition installs credential-free launch shims for provisioned helm and buildctl found on PATH. Bash activation routes bare invocations through the same exec adapter; each invocation resolves current configuration and asks for a fresh session. The prototype does not install those tools. Windows automatic shell shims are not implemented here; explicit launch code is present but native Windows/macOS execution is unqualified.

Before starting a supported command, the compiled adapter sends its directory, tool and arguments to the local agent. The agent either denies or returns a credential endpoint and registry hosts. This is an experimental message shape, not a new versioned public platform schema. The agent is responsible for source admission even for cached inputs. The adapter does not evaluate Rego or parse all native manifests. For an admitted invocation, Oyzu creates temporary Helm/Docker helper configuration, provides a same-image credential helper on the child PATH, and launches the native command. The native helper requests credentials from the session endpoint only when needed. Upstream credentials remain in process memory and helper pipes, not in those configuration files. The native client receives them; this is not an agent-only-secret boundary. The upstream credential enforces read-only access. Each child has separate configuration and session environment. Temporary files are removed after completion, including ordinary child failure. Credential-free shell shim inventory remains in the user tool store. Abruptly killing the parent may leave temporary paths; crash recovery is not qualified. No automatic direct fallback occurs after configured-agent denial or failure. Native stdout/stderr and exit status use the existing exec contract; global --json uses the existing captured-child representation. Helper stdout is the native credential JSON protocol, with only generic failure text on stderr.

The prototype admission response can include projection alongside credentialEndpoint and registries. The agent returns one resolved decision; the client does not combine permissions or evaluate policy. No schema version is introduced. For example (digest placeholders must be replaced): { "credentialEndpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:43199/credential/session", "registries": ["mirror.example.com", "cache.example.com"], "projection": { "imageMappings": [{ "from": "origin.example.com/team/base@sha256:<64-hex-digits>", "to": "mirror.example.com/team/base@sha256:<same-64-hex-digits>" }], "cacheReads": ["cache.example.com/team/build:shared"], "cacheWrites": [] } }
documents.s: Admitted source projection and cache operations

documents.t: With nonempty imageMappings, Oyzu writes a temporary native BuildKit source policy and passes --source-policy-file to buildctl. Exact, fully qualified image references are converted to their admitted destinations. Destinations must be digest-pinned and use an admitted registry authority. A digest-pinned source cannot change digest. Other image sources are denied through BuildKit's native source-policy mechanism. The Dockerfile and shared daemon configuration are not rewritten. Caller-supplied source-policy files conflict with managed admission. The qualified native versions are BuildKit/buildctl 0.25.0 on Linux. This is source substitution, not daemon registry-mirror configuration. The controlled proof has no additional daemon mirror chain: a missing substituted image does not fall back to the original reference. This does not certify arbitrary shared daemon mirrors, redirects, custom frontends or hostile executors. HTTP/Git sources and arbitrary RUN networking are outside this image-source projection. Omitting the projection or using no image mappings retains the earlier credential-helper prototype; it does not claim native image allowlisting. Session admission still occurs before launch, including warm-cache invocations. Native registry cache import/export is separate from image publication: oyzu exec -- buildctl --addr tcp://builder:1234 build \ --frontend dockerfile.v0 --local context=. --local dockerfile=. \ --output type=local,dest=dist \ --import-cache type=registry,ref=cache.example.com/team/build:shared --import-cache type=registry,ref=... requires the exact cacheReads reference; --export-cache type=registry,ref=... requires the exact cacheWrites reference. Both separated and equals-style flags are supported. Missing grants fail before native execution. Local/inline native cache types remain supported; other transports and ambiguous type declarations fail explicitly. Cache grants do not allow image exporters to publish: push=true and type=registry output remain unsupported in this launch path. Publication belongs to oyzu publish. The helper still supplies one identity per registry authority for that invocation. The issuer must choose a narrowly scoped upstream identity covering the admitted operations. When independent credentials cannot fit that native constraint, use separate authorities or invocations; the client does not combine credentials. Cache hits retain their producer/evidence meaning and do not prove tests reran. This adds native BuildKit cache transport, not Oyzu action-cache key generation or cache-trust evaluation.

A Helm response uses helmMappings instead of image/cache grants: { "helmMappings": [{ "from": "origin.example.com/charts/service", "to": "mirror.example.com/charts/service" }] } This projection currently supports one explicit helm pull oci://... reference. Oyzu substitutes only that argument, preserving version and other native arguments, working directory and environment. The destination authority must be admitted. Download the chart and then render the local archive with Helm. No Chart.yaml or lock file is rewritten. Mapped dependency or template operations fail as unsupported; the earlier unmapped helper flows remain distinct. BuildKit source policies never govern Helm retrieval.

OCI intermediate storage is a separate storage purpose from cache or publication. The proof includes a digest-preserving manifest/blob round trip with scoped read/write identities. It does not add an Oyzu intermediate-upload command or implement platform RBAC and catalog binding. Original source, substituted reference, observed request endpoint and digest are distinct facts. The proof records each using its controlled registry observers; this adapter does not yet emit a durable source-evidence report. Native logs are not independent attestations. In particular, a warm cache may produce no new registry request and must not claim a newly observed origin.

Code Meaning and recovery NATIVE_SESSION_CONFIG Move the agent endpoint from project configuration to authorized user/admin configuration NATIVE_SESSION_UNAVAILABLE Start/reconnect the fixture agent; native execution has not started NATIVE_SESSION_DENIED Agent denied the requested context/source; resolve authorization rather than retrying directly NATIVE_SESSION_INVALID, OCI_SESSION_INVALID Agent transport or OCI response/registry addresses are invalid; repair the adapter/agent contract OCI_ROUTING_CONFLICT Correct conflicting source-policy/credential overrides, duplicate mappings, missing authorities or changed pinned digests OCI_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED Use supported retrieval/cache arguments and obtain the specific cache grant; native publication is outside this route OCI_SHIM_INVALID Repair/recreate the generated native shim inventory The prototype requires the configured local agent even for cached content. There is no offline grant implementation. Source validation in the proof uses fixed literal references and fixture policy; arbitrary Dockerfiles, dynamic arguments, transitive dependencies and third-party providers need their own qualification. Native helper selection follows Docker's accepted host-and-port model. No automatic combining of connector permissions occurs. No lock/schema migration is introduced. The new setting is experimental and does not turn on behavior unless configured. The main reference's standalone tool installation and shell lifecycle contracts continue to own those responsibilities. The shared native admission transport now reports NATIVE_SESSION_* for configuration, availability, denial and transport validation. This replaces the prototype transport's earlier OCI_SESSION_* names; OCI response validation and operation-specific diagnostics retain their OCI prefix.

CLI reference Published from the canonical docs/reference/os-package-locks.md file. Features marked experimental remain experimental; check support limitations before relying on them. Experimental. oyzu lock writes debs.lock.yaml and apks.lock.yaml for Docker targets: a reviewed record of every Debian or Alpine package file an image installs, with its URL, version, checksum and Package URL. It implements the observation and lock half of the OS package locks draft. When a target has a lock, oyzu build installs from it: RUN steps see only a loopback snapshot repository that serves the locked files (see Frozen builds). Regenerated metadata and Alpine HTTPS trust are not implemented yet; see Limitations. Tool versions are locked by oyzu pin, not by this command.

Nothing in build.yaml or the Dockerfile changes. For each docker/image target, oyzu lock: Finds the stages that contribute to the final image (through FROM <stage>, COPY --from and RUN --mount=from=) and have at least one RUN. Pins each external base to its index digest and pulls it for this host's platform. A tag keeps the digest already in the lock unless you pass --update. Builds each of those stages once with docker buildx build --load --target, substituting the pinned bases through named build contexts, with the network the host has. This runs the team's own RUN steps. Copies the package database out of each built stage and its base (/var/lib/dpkg/status or /lib/apk/db/installed) without starting either, and takes the difference. That difference is the lock. The RUN shell is never parsed, so a literal apt-get install line, a variable, a heredoc or a copied script all lock the same packages. Asks where each new package comes from: Debian and Ubuntu. apt runs inside the built stage (apt-get update, apt-get download --print-uris, apt-cache madison). apt verifies each repository's signed InRelease against the image's own keyring, so the URL, size and SHA-256 come from verified metadata. Any apt signature warning is a failure (OS_PACKAGE_UNVERIFIED), because apt can report a bad signature as a warning and continue. Alpine. Oyzu reads /etc/apk/repositories and /etc/apk/arch from the built stage, fetches each repository's APKINDEX.tar.gz, finds the exact version, downloads the .apk, checks its size against the index and records its SHA-256. Writes the lock next to the Dockerfile and prints what changed. Package files and repository metadata seen while locking are kept by SHA-256 in a local store (<user data>/os-packages/blobs), ready for prepared frozen builds.

oyzu lock Write missing locks and regenerate stale ones oyzu lock --check Fail if any lock is missing or stale; writes nothing oyzu lock --update Re-observe every lock with fresh bases and no build cache oyzu lock --update api Re-observe only the api target's locks (or name a lock path) oyzu lock --inputs --json List locked packages and bases for Renovate; resolves nothing Every form accepts the global --json flag. $ oyzu lock api-image locked 9 OS packages (2 requested, 7 dependencies) in services/api/debs.lock.yaml note: commit services/api/debs.lock.yaml with your change "Requested" packages are those apt did not mark Auto-Installed, or that are new in Alpine's /etc/apk/world.

Docker with Linux containers and buildx on PATH (Docker Desktop on Windows and macOS, or Docker Engine on Linux), with network access to the base image registry and the distribution mirrors. Standard HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY and SSL_CERT_FILE settings apply to Oyzu's own Alpine downloads. Locks cover this host's architecture only: amd64 or arm64 (x86_64 or aarch64 in Alpine terms). A non-final stage must have a name (AS <name>) to be observed, because BuildKit can only target named stages.

# debs.lock.yaml, written by oyzu lock. Do not edit; run `oyzu lock` after changing the Dockerfile. lockfileVersion: 1 lockfileVendor: oyzu inputDigest: sha256:9f2c… stages: - stage: '0' base: docker.io/library/python@sha256:a6e3… observed: true arches: - arch: amd64 repositories: - repoid: debian-bookworm uri: http://deb.debian.org/debian suite: bookworm release: sha256:61d0… packages: - url: http://deb.debian.org/debian/pool/main/p/postgresql-15/libpq5_15.8-0%2bdeb12u1_amd64.deb repoid: debian-bookworm name: libpq5 evr: 15.8-0+deb12u1 checksum: sha256:7a3c… size: 191234 purl: pkg:deb/debian/libpq5@15.8-0%2Bdeb12u1?arch=amd64&distro=debian-12 sourcerpm: postgresql-15 requested: true stage: '0' url, repoid, checksum and size follow Hermeto's lock schema; name, evr and sourcerpm follow rpm-lockfile-prototype. inputDigest, stages, repositories, purl, requested and stage are Oyzu additions. Unnamed stages are named by index. Packages are sorted by name, version and stage, with no timestamps, so the same inputs and repository state produce the same bytes. release is the SHA-256 of the repository's verified InRelease (apt) or of the APKINDEX.tar.gz the package was found in (apk). url is the live mirror URL apt or apk used; snapshot-service URLs are not written yet. A Dockerfile whose stages use both Debian and Alpine bases gets both files. When an image stops installing one kind of package, oyzu lock removes that file.

A lock is stale when its inputDigest differs from the current inputs. The digest covers, for each locked stage: the FROM references and the stage's instructions up to its last RUN that looks like a package install, including the same span of any stage it starts from; the contents of build-context files that COPY/ADD instructions in that span read, with line endings normalized so Windows and Linux checkouts agree; the stage's pinned base digest; plus global ARG lines and the locked architecture set. A RUN "looks like an install" when it names apt-get, apt, aptitude, dpkg or apk, or runs a file copied earlier in the stage. That is only a hint for where the digest stops: a miss can only make a lock look stale or let a later frozen build fail with OS_PACKAGE_NOT_LOCKED, never produce a wrong lock. Files copied after the last install, such as application source, never make the lock stale. oyzu lock --check is offline. A digest-pinned FROM is compared with the lock's base; a tag keeps the lock's digest for the same repository, so a tag that moves upstream makes the lock behind, not stale. oyzu lock --update picks up the new digest. Stale reasons, in the order checked: a locked stage was removed; its base digest changed; its FROM now names another repository; a stage now installs packages and is in no lock; this host's architecture is not locked; the Dockerfile or the files its install steps copy changed.

{ "format": 1, "mode": "write", "outcome": "written", "locks": [ { "path": "services/api/debs.lock.yaml", "target": "api-image", "reason": "base digest changed for stage 0 (… -> …)", "written": true, "packages": 9, "requested": 2, "changes": [ {"purl": "pkg:deb/debian/libpq5?arch=amd64&distro=debian-12", "stage": "0", "from": "15.7-0+deb12u1", "to": "15.8-0+deb12u1", "requested": true} ] } ] } mode is write, update, check or inputs. outcome is written or current for writes, current or stale for --check, and listed for --inputs. A change with no from is an added package and one with no to was removed. reason is created, update, removed, current or the stale reason. --check entries carry status (current, stale or missing), and for the latter two code: OS_PACKAGE_LOCK_STALE, reason and fix: oyzu lock. A missing entry's path is the target's directory. --inputs entries list dependencies: each base as {depName, currentDigest, datasource: docker} and each package as {depName, currentValue, datasource: deb|apk, registryUrl, purl, requested, stage}. A Debian registryUrl carries Renovate's suite, components and binaryArch parameters.

When a Docker target has debs.lock.yaml or apks.lock.yaml, oyzu build prepares a snapshot repository before execution and never writes the lock: A stale lock fails with OS_PACKAGE_LOCK_STALE. Run oyzu lock first. For the host architecture, Oyzu collects each locked Debian repository's InRelease and the index files it lists (also under by-hash), each Alpine APKINDEX.tar.gz, and every locked package file, from the local store at <user data>/os-packages/blobs. Packages missing from the store are downloaded and must match the lock's checksum and size. apt may keep its lists recompressed, so for each index apt read at lock time (recorded under <user data>/os-packages/indexes; otherwise each component's Packages), a variant the InRelease signs is downloaded by hash when the store holds none, and must match that hash. The prepared tree (index.json mapping URL to SHA-256, plus blobs/) is copied into the BuildKit worker, which has no network, and served by oyzu-docker-snapshot on 127.0.0.1:3128. Its digest is part of the build record (extensions."oyzu.dev/docker".osPackages). RUN steps get host networking inside the worker (--allow network.host, which only reaches loopback there) and http_proxy/https_proxy build arguments pointing at the server. apt verifies the served InRelease with the image's own keyring and every file against its checksums, exactly as at lock time. The server always answers with the full locked file and never with 304 Not Modified, so lists an image already carries (python:*-slim ships an InRelease) cannot stand in for the locked metadata. A request for anything not in the lock gets 404, and a failed build reports it as OS_PACKAGE_NOT_LOCKED naming the package, in the build's error output and its retained log. Targets without a lock build as before. The worker image must include oyzu-docker-snapshot; rebuild the local oyzu-toolchain/docker image (tooling/images/docker-metadata.Dockerfile) after updating Oyzu.

Exit Meaning 0 Locks written or already current; --check found every lock current 1 An operational error, such as a failed observation build 2 Invalid command arguments 3 Configuration or policy validation failed 4 --check found a missing or stale lock

Code When Recovery OS_PACKAGE_LOCK_STALE --check found a missing or stale lock oyzu lock OS_PACKAGE_UNRESOLVABLE apt or apk cannot locate an installed version in the stage's configured repositories, for example a .deb installed by file, or a version replaced upstream between the build and the lookup Install from a configured repository, or run oyzu lock again OS_PACKAGE_UNVERIFIED apt reported a signature problem, or a repository has no signed InRelease Fix the repository's signing key in the image OS_PACKAGE_UNAVAILABLE Oyzu could not download an Alpine index or package, a locked file no longer matches its checksum, or a frozen build needs signed metadata this machine's store does not hold (a lock written elsewhere) Check network and proxy settings, or run oyzu lock --update on this machine OS_PACKAGE_NOT_LOCKED A frozen build's RUN step asked for a package file the lock does not contain oyzu lock --update, or remove the install OS_PACKAGE_METADATA_EXPIRED A frozen build's locked Debian InRelease is past its Valid-Until oyzu lock --update OS_PACKAGE_UPDATE_SELECTOR --update pkg:… selects a single package Update the whole lock or its target A failed observation build reports the last lines of BuildKit's output.

Frozen builds replay original metadata only. Debian metadata past its Valid-Until, or absent from this machine's store, needs regenerated metadata signed with a per-build key (proven in oyzu#152); that is not built yet, so those builds fail with OS_PACKAGE_METADATA_EXPIRED or OS_PACKAGE_UNAVAILABLE. Alpine HTTPS trust. The snapshot server terminates TLS for locked Alpine hosts with a per-build CA, but injecting that CA into RUN steps without leaving it in the image is not implemented, so HTTPS Alpine repositories fail certificate checks in frozen builds. Host architecture only. Frozen builds serve the lock entries for the host architecture. Observation is not recorded through the broker. The observation build has the host's ordinary network, and the lock is cross-checked against the package manager's own metadata rather than against a record of fetched files. Single package updates. --update pkg:deb/debian/libpq5 is refused; updating one package while keeping the others needs observation through the snapshot repository. Not implemented from the draft: input files (debs.in.yaml), --suggest, RPM locks, multiple architectures, snapshot-service URLs and Alpine index signature verification (Oyzu relies on HTTPS for APKINDEX.tar.gz; the size check binds each .apk to the fetched index). Dockerfile reading covers stages, global ARG defaults, line continuations, heredocs and COPY --from/RUN --mount=from=. .dockerignore is not applied to the digest, and files read by RUN --mount=type=bind are not covered. A RUN that runs a file it bind-mounts from the build context still counts as an install, so its stage is observed and locked; a later edit to that file leaves the lock current, and a frozen build refuses any package it adds.

Unit tests cover Dockerfile stages and install hints, package database parsing, PURLs, lock round trips, change reports, staleness reasons and Renovate inputs. tests/integration/os_package_locks.rs drives the compiled CLI against real Docker builds for Debian (OSLOCK-02, 03, 08 and the lock half of 01), a copied-in script (lock half of 06), Alpine (lock half of 07) and a multi-stage build (lock half of 09), plus a frozen Debian build from the snapshot (frozen half of 01) and a bind-mounted script that later asks for an unlocked package, which the frozen build refuses as OS_PACKAGE_NOT_LOCKED naming it (frozen half of 06). They are ignored by default because they need Docker, network and a rebuilt oyzu-toolchain/docker image: oyzu exec -- cargo test --locked --test integration os_package_locks -- --ignored --test-threads 1 All five passed on 2026-10-10 on Windows 11 with Docker Desktop (Linux containers), against a freshly rebuilt oyzu-toolchain/docker:buildkit0.25.0.

CLI reference Published from the canonical docs/reference/plugin-catalog.md file. Features marked experimental remain experimental; check support limitations before relying on them. Experimental. Recognizes a project from a plugin catalog, resolves explicit and detected uses references through one resolver, and shows which builder each target got, why, and how to change it. The design is the draft discovery proposal and package sources; this page records what is implemented (issue #585). Installation, the store and lock records are described in plugin packages. What each release status does to selection, adoption and replay, and the preview's proposed support terms, is in Go builder preview. Nothing here changes a build that has no plugin opt-in, no package binding, no organization catalog and no lock selection: built-in builders keep detecting and building as before, and the build shows no builder selection.
documents.s: Plugin catalog, detection and builder selection

documents.t: The preview builder for Go projects is in the official catalog and on GHCR. In user configuration (never a project file), opt in to preview releases: [plugins] preview = true oyzu build in any Go module now detects go/app from the catalog, acquires oyzu/go 0.1.0-preview.1 from the release's own OCI route in that catalog (ghcr.io/oyzuai/plugins/go@sha256:…, anonymous, signature-verified), records the selection in oyzu.lock and builds with the plugin; Selection shows the source as official default. No binding is needed. A plugins.packages binding still works and takes precedence (a local archive or an OCI source); one whose digest equals the catalog's release is that release's local route.
documents.s: Quick start: the Go builder preview

documents.t: An invocation chooses its catalog snapshot once, and the process keeps it, so two discoveries in one command never see different catalogs. The snapshot is the published catalog of the configured tool index: the official one, or the organization's. No catalog is compiled into the CLI; without a usable published copy there is no snapshot, and the rules under Without a usable catalog apply. Configured tool index (toolIndex.*) plugins.preview Snapshot used Fetched by a real build Official (production trusted root, default identity), any URL on The published official catalog Yes, at most hourly Official off The verified cached published official catalog No toolIndex.url = false any None: there is no catalog No Organization (toolIndex.identity or toolIndex.trustedRoot set) any The organization's published catalog only Yes, at most hourly Every view names the snapshot that decided: official catalog serial 17 or acme catalog serial 3, on the Selection heading, on each target's selected by and source lines, and as label in the JSON records. Published catalog. plugins.json and plugins.json.sigstore.json beside index.json in the configured tool index release, signed by the same identity (tool index). The client verifies the bundle with the index's trusted root and identity, decodes and checks the document with the protocol crate (content digest, structure, limits), refuses it at or after expires_at, and refuses a rollback against the highest verified serial (a lower serial, the same serial with different bytes, or a higher serial generated earlier). The last verified copy lives in <store>/catalogs/plugins/, the rollback floor in <store>/state/plugins/. A copy fetched less than an hour ago is reused without a request. An online build --frozen uses this same metadata refresh rule, so current withdrawals still apply; it neither changes the locked selection nor acquires a missing package from an OCI binding or catalog route. --offline and read-only previews never fetch. A fetched copy that is refused (untrusted, invalid, expired, rolled back) is ignored and the last verified copy stays in force, with its withdrawals and serial floor. If no acceptable copy is usable, there is no catalog and nothing stands in for it; the rules below apply. Organization catalogs are exclusive. With an organization identity the official catalog is never consulted. Without a usable catalog. When no snapshot is usable (an organization catalog, or the official one), the reason decides, the same way for explicit and detected uses: Why there is no snapshot Locked selection Unlocked reference Refused: a fetched copy failed trust, decoding, freshness or rollback and nothing verified is cached; the cached copy fails trust or rollback; or nothing is cached although a serial was verified before (the floor in <store>/state/plugins/ remains) refused before replay, PLUGIN_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE, on every command including --plan refused (PLUGIN_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE) for an organization catalog, with plugins.preview, or when no built-in serves the reference; otherwise built-in Expired: the last verified copy, still the successor of the floor, has expired since its withdrawals and revocations still apply; otherwise the lock replays with the warning PLUGIN_CATALOG_EXPIRED: <ref>: the <label> expired at <expires_at>; replaying oyzu.lock against its withdrawals, but newer withdrawals may be missing. Refresh the catalog …, and JSON records that copy as catalog with expired: true and the same caveat in note. When the refresh of that copy was refused, the warning says the refresh was refused and to fix the catalog source, not to run online as for Refused Absent: nothing published, reachable or cached, and no catalog ever verified in this store (a first run offline, or toolIndex.url = false) replays from oyzu.lock built-in builders only; with plugins.preview on and every target built-in, the Selection section and oyzu plugins explain say no catalog is available (and to run online, or, for toolIndex.url = false, to configure a tool index). Nothing is said while a lock or a binding keeps a plugin in use; the JSON record carries it as catalogNotice A local development binding (plugins.development) or package binding (plugins.packages) for the reference is exempt: it goes on without a usable catalog, but never past a withdrawal or revocation a catalog it does have (the last verified copy, an expired one included) states for the bound release. The refusal names the catalog and says oyzu never falls back to the official catalog (organization) or a bundled one (official; none is compiled in). These rules were agreed with the maintainer for the S3b review. Known gap: a network attacker who blocks the fetch on a store that never verified a catalog yields Absent, so a lock still replays unchecked (#601). The expiry warning is also a note in the Selection section. A build that fails before its receipt (and that section) renders shows it with -v and in --json only, a limitation of the shared receipt. When a refresh is refused or fails and the last verified copy decides, the JSON catalog.note gives the reason and the Selection section adds note using the last verified <label>: <reason>. The official catalog and the preview. The official published catalog lists the Go preview (oyzu/go 0.1.0-preview.1), its references go/app and go/library and the detections go-module (a go.mod with a module directive and no go.work) and go-workspace (a go.work). Without the opt-in a build reads the catalog from the verified cache only, since there is no stable release to find; with the opt-in a real build refreshes it, so its withdrawals apply. A preview is selectable only with plugins.preview, and a withdrawal or revocation refuses the release everywhere, matched by package and version or by root digest. The newest eligible release wins. Nothing is compiled into the CLI as a stand-in. On a machine that has never obtained the catalog (a first run offline, or toolIndex.url = false) there is no snapshot: built-in builders work as before, and a plugin-backed reference needs the catalog or a local binding.

A catalog detection maps observations in a directory to a logical reference. The grammar is fixed by core: exact marker file names, bounded field predicates of JSON, TOML and the module/go/toolchain directives of go.mod (present, equals, prefix), and all/any/not. There are no globs, paths, expressions or commands. Only detections whose reference this invocation could use take part: a reference with an eligible release, a lock selection or a binding. Others add no target. Rules are indexed by marker file name; a directory costs one existence check per marker and is evaluated only against rules whose markers are present. Markers compare case-exactly; a symbolic link is not a marker. Files are read through the discovery source view (contained, at most 4 MiB) once per directory; a malformed file is "no field", never an error. Total work per invocation is bounded: 100,000 directories, 512 parsed files, 32 MiB parsed, 200,000 matcher steps, 1,024 findings. Reaching a bound fails with PLUGIN_DETECTION_INCOMPLETE naming the bound; it never reads as "no match". An explicit build.yaml is the inventory: detection does not run and an incidental file adds no target (PLG-DISC-03). Without one, a directory is a target when a built-in detector or an applicable catalog detection recognizes it, with the existing walk rules (dependency and output directories skipped, nested repositories and build.yaml directories are boundaries). In a directory, every catalog finding and every built-in detection is a candidate. Candidates with different references (two catalog detections, or a catalog go/app beside a built-in rust/app) are PLUGIN_DETECTION_CONFLICT, naming each candidate's evidence and the build.yaml declaration that settles it; oyzu does not guess (PLG-DISC-02). A built-in detection of the same reference is the same candidate. If exactly one candidate is already locked, the lock keeps the target and the others are a note (PLG-DISC-05).

Every target's reference, whether written as uses: in build.yaml, detected by the catalog or recognized by a built-in detector, goes through the same sources in order (PLG-DISC-08): a plugins.development binding (development bindings); a plugins.packages binding. When its digest is the release digest of the catalog's selected release it is that release's local archive route and the selection is the catalog's (official default or company binding), with the package's publisher, name and version checked against the catalog before installation. Any other digest is a local package binding. A binding of a release any consulted catalog withdrew or revoked (matched by root digest before anything is installed, and by digest or package and version once the installer knows the release, which covers an OCI tag) is refused with PLUGIN_RELEASE_WITHDRAWN or PLUGIN_RELEASE_REVOKED before it is recorded or launched; oyzu plugins update reports the same refusal as PLUGIN_UPDATE_REFUSED. A binding never silently changes a lock: when it names a different release than the one oyzu.lock selects, the build fails with PLUGIN_LOCK_MISMATCH until the lock entry is removed; the selection oyzu.lock already holds, replayed and never replaced by a newer catalog, while it stays eligible. A locked release that any consulted catalog withdraws is refused with PLUGIN_RELEASE_WITHDRAWN, and one it revokes with PLUGIN_RELEASE_REVOKED (matched by package and version or by root digest; it never runs), each naming the lock entry to remove so that oyzu build adopts an eligible release. When an organization catalog binds the reference to a different package than the lock (and no local package binding names the locked one), the build fails with PLUGIN_BINDING_CHANGED: a changed company binding is adopted visibly, never replayed silently (PLG-PKG-06). An authentic expired copy also supplies this rebinding refusal; it never supplies an acquisition route; the catalog: the reference's canonical package and profile and its newest eligible release. A release is ineligible when it is withdrawn or revoked, a preview without plugins.preview, unsupported, without protocol generation v1alpha1, without the builder profile, or without a payload for this host's OS, architecture and ABI; the built-in builder serving the reference, if any. A reference no builder serves fails with PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE and the catalog's reason. A catalog-selected release with no binding is acquired by a real oyzu build from the OCI route in its verified catalog entry, through the installer an OCI binding uses: anonymous, by the listed root digest, with the same package, platform and withdrawal checks, and recorded in oyzu.lock as exactly that root. With an existing lock and an empty plugin store, an online, non-frozen oyzu build acquires the exact locked digest from that release's own entry in the current verified snapshot, even when a newer release is listed. It never rewrites the lock. Withdrawals and revocations are checked before routing; an unlisted digest, or a Refused, Absent or Expired catalog, supplies no route. Existing installed releases retain the replay rules above. A release already in the store is reused without a request, and is not verified again. Route trust follows the package identity (decision of 2026-10-20). A release of a package of the official publisher oyzu (such as oyzu/go) must carry a signature from the fixed official signer (the plugin-release.yml workflow on main, GitHub-hosted runner), verified against Sigstore's production trusted root, on whatever registry the catalog routes it through: the official ghcr.io/oyzuai/plugins/<name>, or a company mirror an organization catalog lists. A mirror therefore has to serve the release's signature referrers as well as its root, manifests and blobs, and the root it serves must hash to the digest the catalog lists. Nothing in a catalog or in configuration can name another signer or trusted root for it, so a company catalog cannot pass off its own build as oyzu/go. A route in the official namespace always requires the official signer. A release of a package of any other publisher (such as acme/go on a company registry) is trusted by its digest, which the signed catalog lists, as a digest binding is; no signature is requested. A refused mirror reports PLUGIN_SIGNATURE_MISSING (no signature referrer), PLUGIN_SIGNATURE_INVALID (no signature verifies for the official signer against the production root) or PLUGIN_PACKAGE_DIGEST (other bytes under the listed root), and installs and records nothing. The real official signature through a mirror is proved by the mirror qualification; the loopback registry tests cannot hold a production signature and prove the refusals. Routes come only from the verified catalog, never from project files. A release with no OCI route (an HTTPS layout-archive route is not acquired from yet), or any release under --offline that is not in the store, fails with PLUGIN_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE naming the binding that supplies it; a route that cannot be used (unreachable, incomplete, serving other bytes than the listed root) fails with PLUGIN_ROUTE_FAILED and installs and records nothing (only for access: an unreachable or incomplete registry, or an unusable listed address; a signature, digest or package failure keeps its own code and advice). A catalog-only builder (a reference no built-in builder serves, PLG-DISC-04) runs with only the tools its package manifest requires. Only a real oyzu build adopts or installs. Every other command (build --plan, --check, run, discover, …) replays the lock and the store; an unadopted catalog selection there is PLUGIN_NOT_ADOPTED: the catalog selects <package> <version> (release …) for <reference> … this command downloads, installs, launches and writes nothing (PLG-DISC-06). Help, --version, shell activation and oyzu exec never load a catalog or select a builder (PLG-DISC-07).

plugins.preview = true makes preview releases eligible. It is accepted only from user, machine or administrative configuration, never from a project file, oyzu.local.toml or a profile (CONFIG_SCOPE), because it selects code to run: oyzu config set --global plugins.preview true

A build with a plugin-backed target shows the builder selection in the Selection section, after Prepare (so tools are known) and before Plan. When the build adopted a selection or installed a package, each such target gets the full record: -- Selection --- official catalog serial 18 ok go/app project oyzu/go 0.1.0-preview.1 (adopted) selected by go.mod module (rule go-module, official catalog serial 18) source official default · from official catalog serial 18 · preview release (plugins.preview) package installed now · sha256:0382c192…ee48 · 710.6 KiB · from /home/me/go-0.1.0-preview.1.tar.gz lock recorded in oyzu.lock now; review and commit the diff tool go 1.27.2 · installed now · go.mod requires go >=1.22; nothing pins it not what you wanted? not a go/app target? Declare the targets you want in build.yaml; undeclared directories add none build.yaml: {builds: {project: {uses: <builder>, path: .}}} another implementation of go/app? Bind its package for this reference (or use your organization's catalog) and select again oyzu config set --global --json-value 'plugins.packages."go/app"' '{"archive":"<path>","sha256":"<digest>"}' && rm oyzu.lock undo this adoption: revert oyzu.lock and this reference's settings (plugins.preview is the global preview opt-in) rm oyzu.lock && oyzu config unset --global 'plugins.packages."go/app"' && oyzu config set --global plugins.preview false another go version? Pin it in oyzu.toml oyzu pin go@<version> When nothing changed, each plugin-backed target is one line: -- Selection --- official catalog serial 18 reused go/app project oyzu/go 0.1.0-preview.1 (locked) Field Meaning selected by uses in build.yaml, the catalog detection's evidence and rule with the snapshot, or the built-in detector source official default, company binding (an organization catalog), local package binding, local development binding, or oyzu.lock (a locked selection no current source explains), with the snapshot that listed the release; preview release (plugins.preview) with the opt-in, or prerelease version when a local binding supplied a prerelease without it package installed now with release digest, archive size and the local route, or reused from the store lock adopted now (a reviewable oyzu.lock diff), replayed, or not locked (development) tool each tool this target requires (not every tool of the build), with version, whether installed now, and why: the native requirement and that nothing pins it, or where it is pinned remedies one copyable line per case; the build.yaml line lists the other detected targets when there are any. other-implementation and undo change only this reference's binding (plugins.packages."<reference>"); plugins.preview has no per-reference form, so undoing a catalog preview turns the global opt-in off. For a selection locked earlier, the line ends with oyzu plugins update <reference> Targets using built-in builders are not listed. Notes (for example a competing detection kept out by a lock, or why an expired catalog was used) follow the targets. Without color the marks are words (ok, reused). --json records the same typed result as the build manifest's extensions["oyzu.dev/plugin-selection"]: {"catalog":{"label":"official catalog serial 17","source":"fetched","authority":"oyzu", "official":true,"serial":17,"generatedAt":"…","expiresAt":"…","expired":false, "contentDigest":"sha256:…","documentDigest":"sha256:…","url":"https://github.com/…","note":null}, "catalogChoice":"published","preview":true,"changed":true,"notes":[], "targets":[{"target":"project","path":".","reference":"go/app", "decision":{"kind":"detected","rule":"go-module","evidence":["go.mod module"], "catalog":"official catalog serial 18"}, "source":"official-default","authority":"oyzu", "catalog":"official catalog serial 18","package":"oyzu/go", "version":"0.1.0-preview.1","release":"sha256:…","preview":true, "state":"adopted","installedNow":true,"size":727700,"route":"/home/me/…", "executableDigest":"sha256:…","packageBinding":true, "tools":[{"tool":"go","id":"oyzu:go","requirement":"go.mod requires go >=1.22", "reason":["Go compiler for selected build stages"],"pinned":false}], "remedies":[{"case":"wrong-ecosystem","summary":"…","action":"…"}, {"case":"other-implementation","summary":"…","action":"…"},{"case":"undo","summary":"…","action":"…"}, {"case":"tool-version","summary":"another go version? Pin it in oyzu.toml","action":"oyzu pin go@<version>"}]}]} catalogChoice (why the snapshot) is published, no-index, official-unavailable or organization. tools lists the target's own tool requirements, added once the build has collected them; the resolved versions stay in the build's tool records. The record is crate::plugins::resolve::Explanation. oyzu plugins explain shows the same record after the fact without adopting, installing or launching anything; only there state can also be not-adopted or not-installed.

Adoption happens only in a real build and always appears as an oyzu.lock diff. There are no prompts. Each wrong choice has a fix, verified through the compiled CLI after applying it (verification): Wrong choice Fix Wrong ecosystem from an incidental file Declare the targets you want in build.yaml (the printed line); the incidental directory adds no target and its builder is never acquired Right ecosystem, unwanted implementation The printed line binds another package for this reference only (oyzu config set --global --json-value 'plugins.packages."<reference>"' …) and reverts the lock this build wrote; for an older lock, remove its [[plugin]] entry, then build Right builder, wrong tool version oyzu pin <tool>@<version> writes the pin to oyzu.toml Ambiguous evidence (npm and pnpm lockfiles; two catalog detections) Discovery stops with a focused conflict naming the smallest build.yaml selector; nothing is guessed or installed Undo an adoption The printed line: git checkout -- oyzu.lock, or rm oyzu.lock when this build created it, then this reference's plugins.packages entry when it supplied the bytes, and plugins.preview for a catalog preview (global: it has no per-reference form)

Code Cause Recovery PLUGIN_DETECTION_CONFLICT Candidates with different references (catalog detections, or a catalog detection and a built-in one) match a directory Declare the target with uses: in build.yaml PLUGIN_RELEASE_WITHDRAWN, PLUGIN_RELEASE_REVOKED A consulted catalog (an expired copy included) withdrew or revoked the locked release, or the release a plugins.packages binding names: by digest before anything is installed, and by digest or package and version once the installer knows the release, which covers an OCI tag. A bound release is refused before it is recorded or launched Run oyzu plugins update REFERENCE (it needs a binding or the store to supply the replacement), or remove the named [[plugin]] entry and build, to adopt an eligible release; for a binding, bind an eligible release or run the oyzu config unset --global … line the error prints. The refused bytes stay in the store when they had to be fetched to be identified (a tag, or a package refused by package and version); oyzu plugins list marks them (withdrawn) or (revoked), and nothing can select them PLUGIN_BINDING_CHANGED The organization catalog binds the reference to another package than the lock Remove the named [[plugin]] entry and build to adopt the new binding visibly PLUGIN_LOCK_MISMATCH A plugins.packages binding names another release than the lock Remove the lock entry, or restore the binding PLUGIN_DETECTION_INCOMPLETE A matcher work bound was reached Declare the targets in build.yaml PLUGIN_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE The catalog selects a release that is not installed and has no OCI route, or --offline forbids its route Run online, or bind the archive with the release digest (plugins.packages) PLUGIN_ROUTE_FAILED The release's catalog route could not be used (registry unreachable or not holding the release, or an unusable listed address); the cause follows. A signature, digest or package failure keeps its own code Fix access to the registry, or bind the package; nothing was installed or recorded PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE No builder serves the reference; the catalog says why (for example preview only) Opt in, or bind a package PLUGIN_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE No usable snapshot and the catalog was refused, or an unlocked reference met an expired one (see Without a usable catalog) Restore access to the catalog, or select a local binding; oyzu never falls back to another catalog for the reference PLUGIN_CATALOG_EXPIRED (warning) A lock replayed against an expired catalog's withdrawals Refresh the catalog with an online oyzu build; if the refresh was refused, fix the catalog source PLUGIN_CATALOG_INVALID, _EXPIRED, _ROLLBACK Reasons inside the above PLUGIN_PACKAGE_MISMATCH The archive is not the catalog's package and version Bind the right archive PLUGIN_NOT_ADOPTED A non-build command met an unadopted selection Run oyzu build

Only the OCI route is acquired from; an HTTPS layout-archive route is not. Locked acquisition needs a current verified catalog listing the exact root, or an explicit binding. Without either, a missing release remains PLUGIN_LOCK_UNUSABLE; Refused catalogs remain PLUGIN_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE. --frozen and --offline never acquire from a catalog route. oyzu plugins current and explain install nothing and describe the pending acquisition; build --plan never downloads and stops with PLUGIN_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE. See the lock replay qualification for the evidence and what is not proved. A route for a package of another publisher carries no signer identity: the signed catalog's digest is its trust. An official package needs the official signature on every route. Without plugins.preview the official published catalog is not refreshed by builds; there is no --refresh yet. The published entry lists the platforms the release was built for (darwin, linux and windows); only linux/amd64 musl is proved end to end. @vN major selectors in uses, revocation of installed copies and policy admission are not implemented. Updates are oyzu plugins update. oyzu config validate checks declared uses against built-in builders only, so it rejects a catalog-only reference a build would accept. Windows and macOS are untested.

Unit tests: src/plugins/catalog.rs (a published official catalog is the only snapshot; without one there is none; a refused refresh stays a refusal), src/plugins/resolve.rs (a published preview is selectable only with the opt-in; an official withdrawal by package and version, or by root digest, refuses the release and removes its detections), src/plugins/matcher.rs (go.mod directives, exact markers, symbolic links, JSON/TOML fields, malformed files, budget exhaustion). Compiled-CLI tests tests/integration/plugin_catalog.rs, with an organization catalog served over loopback and signed by a test-only Sigstore instance and a stand-in plugin: detected selection, --plan without acquisition, missing route, locked replay against a newer release and a competing detector, unlocked conflict (PLG-DISC-02, 05, 06); explicit and detected references give identical lock records (PLG-DISC-08); an explicit build.yaml keeps an incidental Go module out and nothing is installed (PLG-DISC-03); preview needs the user-scope opt-in and a project cannot set it; a catalog update adds a catalog-only builder (PLG-DISC-04); a refused organization catalog does not fall back; help, --version and exec neither fetch nor select (PLG-DISC-07); npm and pnpm lockfiles name the package-manager selector (PLG-DISC-02). Route acquisition, tests/integration/plugin_oci.rs (catalog_routes, a signed organization catalog and a loopback registry, no binding): adopt, lock and --frozen replay without the registry; a binding keeps precedence; a withdrawn release is never fetched; a route serving other bytes, an unreachable route and --offline fail without installing or recording; an official package (oyzu/go) through a company mirror is refused without the official signature (unsigned, signed by the company, signed with the official identity by another Sigstore instance, other bytes under the listed root) on first adoption, committed-lock replay and oyzu plugins update, in human and JSON output, while a plugins.packages binding keeps precedence and an installed release is reused without a request. Unit tests in src/plugins/resolve.rs and src/tools/plugin_package/oci.rs (route selected, no OCI route, offline, withdrawn and revoked, precedence, root mismatch, and the signer of a catalog route by package identity). The real official signature through a mirror: tests/integration/plugin_mirror.rs, ignored by default because it copies the published release from GHCR (see the mirror qualification). End to end on linux/amd64 (2026-10-18) with the compiled CLI, the real preview Go plugin, scratch XDG directories (so the default store is scratch; oyzu pin has no --store), scratch user configuration (plugins.preview = true plus the local archive route) and a fresh Git checkout of examples/builds/go-app/project, with no plugin installed: oyzu build refreshed and verified the live official catalog (serial 17, production Sigstore trust root), detected go/app from the bundled preview source of that day (since replaced by the published catalog), installed oyzu/go 0.1.0-preview.1 and Go 1.27.2, showed the full Selection record, wrote the [[plugin]] entry (git status: new oyzu.lock) and produced dist/project/artifacts/project-0.0.0-dev.…, which prints Hello, Oyzu! (PLG-DISC-01). The printed undo line (rm oyzu.lock && oyzu config set --global plugins.preview false && oyzu config unset --global plugins.packages) run as printed: the next build used the built-in builder, showed no builder selection and wrote no [[plugin]] entry. Opting in again re-adopted the release from the store with no archive route; after committing the lock the rebuild showed the one-line form, and --json carried the same record (state: locked). oyzu pin go@1.24.5 wrote the pin to oyzu.toml; the next build installed and used Go 1.24.5 with the locked plugin, and the artifact ran. Binding another package of go/app was refused against the lock (PLUGIN_LOCK_MISMATCH); after removing the [[plugin]] entry the build adopted it as a local package binding. In a checkout with image/Dockerfile and an incidental tools/go.mod, the build adopted go/app for project-tools and printed build.yaml: {builds: {project-image: {uses: docker/image, path: image}}}; with that file, a build with a fresh store planned only project-image, installed no plugin and wrote no lock (PLG-DISC-03).

CLI reference Published from the canonical docs/reference/plugin-development.md file. Features marked experimental remain experimental; check support limitations before relying on them. A local development binding makes oyzu build and oyzu run use an external builder plugin executable in place of a built-in builder profile. It exists to develop and compare external builders against the draft plugins-v1alpha1 builder contract before plugin packages, sources and locks exist. Two plugins are developed this way: oyzu-plugin-go, the Go host lane extracted from the built-in Go builder (Milestone A of issue #582), and oyzu-plugin-node, the built-in Node builder's native npm application lane (slice N1 of Node externalization, issues #743 and #772). Without a binding nothing changes: every builder id resolves to its built-in builder exactly as before.

Experimental, for builder development. The setting, the protocol and the recorded fields are draft and may change in place. Native host lane only. A bound target builds with native host tools through native-admission, native-build, native-test and task-command. A raw executable binding cannot establish an execution-platform payload for captured builds. That path requires an admitted multi-platform package with captured-plan and exact engine assets; otherwise it fails before preparation or build actions. There is no fallback to the built-in builder. When the plugin declines a target for the native host lane, the failure carries the plugin's own reason (see Failures and recovery). Replaces a built-in profile. The bound id must be one a built-in builder serves (for example go/app). Detection, builder settings and dependency providers stay with that built-in builder; tasks, requirements, admission, build, test and task-command answers come from the plugin. No plugin packages. There is no download, signature, manifest admission or oyzu.lock entry. The executable is local development content, recorded by path and SHA-256 digest only.

An Oyzu CLI built from a revision containing this feature. A plugin executable. Build the Go or Node plugin from this repository: oyzu exec -- cargo build --locked -p oyzu-plugin-go --features plugin # target/debug/oyzu-plugin-go (oyzu-plugin-go.exe on Windows) oyzu exec -- cargo build --locked -p oyzu-plugin-node --features plugin # target/debug/oyzu-plugin-node (oyzu-plugin-node.exe on Windows) The executable requires the plugin feature so the repository's own cli build, which collects every enabled workspace binary, never ships it. Check the plugin against the contract with its conformance test, which runs the canonical requests through core's process host against temporary Go projects: oyzu exec -- cargo test --locked -p oyzu-plugin-go --features plugin The Node plugin's tests (--features plugin) also drive the compiled CLI, so build it first (oyzu exec -- cargo build --locked --bin oyzu) or set OYZU_CLI. CI does not run them. The native tools the target needs, provisioned as usual. Core resolves, locks and installs oyzu:go or oyzu:node from the plugin's requirements answer, as it does for the built-in builder. For a verified, locked package instead of a local path, see plugin packages.

Add the binding to your user configuration (~/.config/oyzu/config.toml on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support/Oyzu/config.toml on macOS, %APPDATA%\Oyzu\config.toml on Windows, or the file OYZU_USER_CONFIG names): [plugins.development] "go/app" = "/home/me/src/oyzu/target/debug/oyzu-plugin-go" "node/app" = "/home/me/src/oyzu/target/debug/oyzu-plugin-node" Then build or run tasks as usual in a Go project: oyzu build oyzu build --full oyzu run test oyzu run build The build shows the core-allocated plugin output directory in its build command (go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -o .oyzu/native/plugin/…). The Context facts in dist/logs/events.jsonl include Plugins go/app → local development <path> (sha256:…), and the retained inventory records {"reference","content":"local-development","executable","digest"} for each binding. The executable that runs is a private per-invocation copy of the file whose digest was recorded, and the plan, envelope and manifest carry extensions["oyzu.dev/plugins"]; see plugin packages. A Node project builds when it is an npm application declared uses: node/app in build.yaml whose own build script writes dist; see the Node plugin for what it runs and how it differs from the built-in builder. Remove the table (or the entry) to return to the built-in builder.

Key Type Default Scopes plugins.development table of builder id to absolute executable path none user, machine, administrative Keys are short builder references without a major version (go/app, not go@1/app or an OCI reference). Values are absolute paths. At most 64 entries. The setting selects executable code, so project oyzu.toml, oyzu.local.toml and profile overlays are refused with CONFIG_SCOPE: plugins.development is not permitted in this scope. Administrative constraints apply as for any setting. In CI, user configuration is excluded as usual; a machine-scope binding still applies. The table is atomic: a later source replaces the whole table. Bindings are resolved once per invocation, before targets are discovered. A missing or unreadable executable, or an id no built-in builder serves, fails discovery with PLUGIN_BINDING_INVALID.

Decision Owner Detection, with validation (non-empty options refused), settings Core and the built-in builder Conventional tasks, tool requirements, host admission, build commands, artifacts, test command and reports, workspace expansion Plugin Build version Core resolves it (versioning owner) and sends it; the plugin must echo it Output directory Core allocates .oyzu/native/plugin/<fresh> in the target's private execution directory per build Project-written outputs (origin: target) The plugin names the path the project's own script writes (a Node dist); core checks it, retires earlier output in the private workspace before authored operations and collects what the build wrote (below) Report directory Core sends .oyzu/plugin-reports and binds each argument naming <report_dir>/<file> to the run's fresh report directory before execution Requirement origin digests Core rereads the cited file and refuses a mismatch task-command observations Core checks the tool is one the builder admits (oyzu:go) and that argv[0] is that tool's command, runs it once on the task's provisioned PATH, then re-invokes the plugin Scheduling, execution, artifact collection, report gates Core, unchanged
documents.s: What core does and what the plugin does

documents.t: A plugin whose ecosystem's build script decides where its output goes, as npm run build writes dist, cannot steer that output into the core-allocated output directory. Its native-build or captured-plan result instead marks the artifact "origin": "target" with a target-relative source, and its build operation runs the selected task's own command (core sends it as input.task.argv): {"name": "primary", "producer": "build", "kind": "directory", "filename": "application-1.4.0", "media_type": "application/octet-stream", "source": "dist", "executable": false, "origin": "target"} The default origin, output-dir, is omitted when encoded, so an existing plugin's results (the Go plugin's) are unchanged. Core enforces, before any build action runs: Rule Refused with The source names something below the target: not ., and no segment that starts or ends with a dot (.git, .oyzu), is node_modules (any case) or is a Windows device name (con, nul, COM1.txt) PLUGIN_OPERATION_FAILED: … invalid result Sources are unique, ignoring case PLUGIN_OPERATION_FAILED: … invalid result The source neither equals, contains nor lies inside output_dir PLUGIN_OPERATION_FAILED: … overlaps the output directory The source neither equals, contains nor lies inside a file or directory of the target's frozen source selection, ignoring case PLUGIN_ARTIFACT_REFUSED: … overlaps the frozen source selection at <path> No existing segment of the path is a symbolic link or reparse point, and none above the last is a file PLUGIN_ARTIFACT_REFUSED: artifact … names … with the cause Then core retires the path: whatever exists there is renamed into a fresh core-owned directory beside the output directory, never deleted in place, and is discarded with that directory after collection. The build plan records each retired path under extensions["oyzu.dev/retired-outputs"], for example {"web":[{"artifact":"primary","path":"dist","previous":false}]}. A build whose script writes nothing fails with native artifact collection failed rather than republishing an earlier output. Collection then applies the usual rules (no links, no reserved names, a directory inventory or a regular file).
